items.prompt: In a route planning system, a dispatch planner must compute a route. expensive recomputation must not starve urgent dispatch requests The design review focuses on access-pattern-first data modeling. constraints: expensive recomputation must not starve urgent dispatch requests
Transfer the ownership and failure rule, then re-evaluate the changed workload rather than copying a product solution.
The primary decision is model data from dominant read and write access patterns plus invariants, then choose representation..
Keep the scenario provider-neutral and do not rely on a canonical product solution.

options.text: Model data from dominant read and write access patterns plus invariants, then choose representation. In this transfer case for route planning, the access path and invariant determine keys, locality, indexes, and whether denormalization is justified. The owner must also make a computational hotspot observable rather than silently passing it to another layer.
Choose the nearest familiar component and let each caller decide access-pattern-first data modeling independently, without a shared owner or failure contract.
Add replication, caching, retries, or asynchronous buffering immediately, even though the scenario has not shown that mechanism is the limiting constraint.
Keep the happy path and treat a computational hotspot as an operational exception that the caller can resolve manually.
Select a named cloud or vendor product first and infer the workload, ownership, and guarantee from that product's defaults.

Details.scenarioApplication: For route planning, the decision keeps expensive recomputation must not starve urgent dispatch requests attached to the owner that can observe the state. The design treats a computational hotspot as a named failure path.
Details.errorCorrection: The distractors either make the boundary unowned, add unmeasured complexity, ignore recovery, or replace mechanism reasoning with provider trivia. Transfer the ownership and failure rule, then re-evaluate the changed workload rather than copying a product solution.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not reduce “Access-pattern-first data modeling” to terminology recall. Choose storage from access patterns and invariants, not from data labels alone; separate source-of-truth storage from derived indexes and caches. The trade-off is that explicit ownership and evidence may require a narrower contract or an operational signal, but that cost is preferable to silently violating the stated guarantee.
Details.ownership: The service or boundary that owns the relevant state and can enforce access-pattern-first data modeling must own the decision; callers coordinate through the contract.
Details.transfer: Carry the ownership and failure rule into a new domain, then re-check the changed workload, guarantee, and recovery requirement.
